title: Chocolate orange shortbread
subtitle: a cocoa and orange zest shortbread dipped in dark chocolate
excerpt: Chocolate orange shortbread has cocoa powder worked into the base dough and orange zest for fragrance. The biscuits are stamped out, baked until just set, and then dipped halfway into melted dark chocolate once cool. The result is a two-tone biscuit with a sandy, crumbly texture and a bitter-sweet chocolate finish.
sourceNotes: Chocolate orange shortbread, a British home-baking confectionery biscuit. Method from standard contemporary British patisserie.

glossaryTerms.definition: Shortbread made with a proportion of cocoa powder in place of some of the flour, giving a chocolate-flavoured biscuit with the same sandy, crumbling texture as plain shortbread.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze un-dipped biscuits. Dip in chocolate after thawing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 2 weeks.

content.text: in place of some of the flour. The orange zest goes into the dough raw: the flavour bakes in gently. Once cooled, the biscuits are dipped in melted chocolate and left on baking parchment to set. Use 70% dark chocolate for the best contrast with the sweet biscuit.

Beat the butter and icing sugar together until pale and creamy. Beat in the orange zest. Add the flour, cocoa, and salt and mix until a soft dough forms. Flatten to a disc, wrap in cling film, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Line two baking trays with baking parchment.
Roll the dough on a lightly floured surface to about 5 mm thick. Stamp out with a 6 cm round or fluted cutter and place on the prepared trays. Re-roll offcuts once.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until set and slightly darker at the edges. Leave to cool completely on the trays; they firm as they cool.

Melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water. Dip each biscuit halfway in and shake gently to remove any drips. Place on a sheet of baking parchment to set at room temperature, about 30 minutes.

attrs.problem: Biscuits spreading and losing their shape during baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid soft or warm butter in the dough; the butter must be well incorporated but not greasy.
attrs.fix: Refrigerate the shaped biscuits on the tray for 15 minutes before baking.

attrs.problem: Chocolate dip is thick and gloopy rather than smooth
attrs.avoid: Avoid overheating the chocolate; water contact or excessive heat makes it seize.
attrs.fix: Add a teaspoon of neutral oil to the melted chocolate and stir to thin it to a dipping consistency.
